issues.description: Docstring deprecation directive contains 'stlib' typo and should read 'stdlib'.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged the misspelled reference to the replacement API in the .. deprecated:: 4.3 directive. Specifications live in the docstring; a typo in the substitution guidance weakens the deprecation contract. Trivial to fix while the directive is being added.

issues.description: Deprecation test does not exercise the stderr-redirect substitution path.
issues.detail: The deprecation message promises substitution by both contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr, but the new test only verifies stdout redirection plus a warning match. Add a stderr case to confirm the full contract being deprecated still behaves identically, and consider exception-path restoration.

issues.description: Deprecation note should mention that replacing redirected requires nesting two contextlib managers.
issues.detail: falcon.testing.redirected swaps both stdout and stderr in a single context, while contextlib exposes redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr as separate managers. The migration guidance in the deprecation message should note that callers using both streams must nest two contexts to preserve the original postcondition.

synthesis.summary: Panel consensus: ACCEPT with trivial fixups. The change is a clean, scoped, contract-preserving deprecation that wraps the existing generator with a @deprecated decorator, updates internal callers, adds a news fragment, and includes a test exercising the warning. Substitutability with contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr holds. Three minor issues remain: a 'stlib' typo in the Sphinx directive, the test only covers the stdout path while the deprecation promises both streams, and the migration guidance should note that replacing redirected requires nesting two contextlib managers.
